title: Necessity and Sufficiency for Explaining Text Classifiers: A Case Study in Hate Speech Detection
measurement_description: Bias against Muslims in hate speech detection models, evaluated through necessity and sufficiency scores of identity terms.
findings: The study found that several hate speech detection models exhibited significant bias, where the mere presence of the term 'Muslims' was highly sufficient to trigger a 'hate speech' classification, even in neutral or positive contexts. This over-sensitivity led to high false positive rates for non-hateful sentences mentioning Muslims. The proposed necessity and sufficiency metrics were effective at quantifying and explaining this bias.
references: Amina Adadi and Mohammed Berrada. 2018. Peeking inside the black-box: A survey on explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). IEEE Access, 6:52138–52160.
